chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha'i, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever wants to travel, it is better for him to go on a trip on Saturdays because if a stone becomes separated from the mountain, God will return it to its place on that day. It is better for those who have some need, to ask for it on a Tuesday since that is the day on which God softened iron for David (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended days for travel and fulfilling needs in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this narration underscores the cosmological significance of days in Shia tradition, linking Saturday’s stability to the softening of iron for Prophet David and Tuesday’s efficacy to the same divine favor. The mention of stones returning to their place on Saturday reflects a belief in the unique metaphysical properties of specific weekdays, while Tuesday is highlighted as an auspicious time for seeking needs, echoing the Quranic account of God softening iron for David (21:80).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-70 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha’ee, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

Whoever wants to travel, it is better for him to go on a trip on Saturdays because if a stone becomes separated from the mountain, God will return it to its place on that day. It is better for those who have some need, to ask for it on a Tuesday since that is the day on which God softened iron for David (MGB).”
